lane: S3 THERMAL-CONDUIT / RING-HABITAT EMISSION (self-declared; no method paragraph was ever supplied - IR-10)
hypothesis: Off-catalogue fault density concentrates in the 3-30 px ring around the mapped catalogue (damage-zone splays and continuations) rather than in thermal anomalies or in blind uniform coverage; a clean-contamination blue-noise emission weighted to that ring covers more hidden truth per dot than any registry placement, and the thermal-well/spring field (GDR 1391) adds no further enrichment (measured negative).
mechanism: m(d) = exp(-(d-12)^2/(2*10^2)) + 0.20 for d > 3 px from labels.tif (0 otherwise); mixture-sampled blue-noise (50% ring-rank / 50% seeded uniform floor), min-sep 3 px, N = 37,654 (champion-matched budget), binary 1-cell emission, hard 3 px collar off the bridge catalogue. No competition label is read; the catalogue is a repeller only.
named_non_fault_process: Alluvial-fan toes and playa-margin reworking mimic fault-adjacent topography in the ring, and basin-fill groundwater advection mimics the thermal field. The 3 px collar removes mapped mimics; the uniform floor bounds the unmapped ones. Not fully removed.

exp1_share_sweep.finding: Greedy acceptance depends only on rank, so all thermal share values > 0 give identical dots; with a proper seeded uniform control the thermal-ranked placement LOSES on both instruments (IHR 0.0287 vs 0.0439; SGMC 0.0329 vs 0.0750). Verdict: thermal-conduit hypothesis NEGATIVE as a placement prior.

exp2_placement_decision.finding: ring-binary-37654 wins instrument consensus (IHR 0.0597, SGMC 0.0770). N=24,000 is negative on both instruments. plateau1 soft emission is a split verdict (IHR 0.0312 / SGMC 0.0925): soft axis stays UNTESTED for the leaderboard.
